source: Kadavath et al. (2022) Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
finding: Larger models are well calibrated on multiple-choice and true/false questions when the format is right. Models can judge their own sampled answers with P(True).
numbers: 52B model; P(True) tested 20-shot on TriviaQA, Lambada, Arithmetic, GSM8k, Codex HumanEval; calibration measured by ECE with 10 bins and by AUROC.
limits: Calibration is good in a favourable format only; replacing an option with None of the Above harms performance and calibration.
agent_relevance: A first-order self-check (P(True)) can work as a cheap monitor of own answers. Use true/false format, not open verbal ratings.

source: Kadavath et al. (2022) Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
finding: Showing the model several of its own samples before asking P(True) improves self-evaluation. Keeping only answers with P(True) > 0.5 raises accuracy on all five sampling tasks.
numbers: Figure 1: accuracy gain conditioned on P(True) > 0.5 on GSM8k, Arithmetic, TriviaQA, Lambada, Codex.
limits: Single 52B family from one lab; sampled at unit temperature.
agent_relevance: Sample-then-judge (compare several own samples) fits a verify step better than judging one answer alone.

source: Kadavath et al. (2022) Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
finding: P(IK) (probability I know the answer, with no proposed answer) is learned by finetuning. It partly generalises across tasks but is badly calibrated on new tasks. It rises when source text or hints are in context.
numbers: AUROC of P(IK) rises with model size; calibration poor out of distribution; increases with hints on GSM8k.
limits: Needs finetuning; not a prompt-only ability.
agent_relevance: Pre-answer 'do I know this' signals are weak without training. Do not trust a prompted 'I know' flag out of domain (G10).

source: Lin, Hilton, Evans (2022) Teaching models to express their uncertainty in words
finding: GPT-3, finetuned, outputs verbal confidence ('90% confidence') that is calibrated on CalibratedMath and stays moderately calibrated under distribution shift. It tracks its own uncertainty and does not just copy human examples.
numbers: CalibratedMath suite; scored by MSE of stated confidence against correctness; verbalized and logit-based uncertainty both generalise.
limits: Requires finetuning on the calibration task; GPT-3 era model; arithmetic domain.
agent_relevance: Verbal confidence can be learned, but the base model does not give it for free.

source: Xiong et al. (2024) Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation
finding: Plain verbalized confidence is overconfident and poor at telling right from wrong. GPT-4 has lower ECE but weak failure prediction.
numbers: Five LLMs, eight tasks; GPT-4 average AUROC 62.7% (chance 50%); GPT-3, GPT-3.5, Vicuna average ECE above 0.377; AUROC gain about 22.2% from GPT-3 to GPT-4.
limits: Black-box API setting; verbalized values cluster in the 80 to 100 percent range.
agent_relevance: Do not use a stated confidence number as a gate. It carries little discrimination (G10).

source: Xiong et al. (2024) Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation
finding: Better calibration from prompt tricks can be an illusion. CoT lowers ECE only because accuracy rises while confidence stays at 80-100 percent.
numbers: GSM8K with CoT: GPT-4 accuracy 93.6%, ECE 0.064 by giving 100% confidence to everything, so AUROC stays near chance.
limits: Shows ECE alone is a misleading metric; need AUROC.
agent_relevance: When testing a self-report in our harness, measure discrimination (AUROC), not only calibration error.

source: Xiong et al. (2024) Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation
finding: Consistency across several sampled answers beats a single verbalized number for failure prediction. Sampling more answers helps, with M up to 13 tested.
numbers: One reported case: AUROC moved from 54.8% (near random) to 92.7% with multi-response aggregation; white-box vs black-box gap 0.522 to 0.605 AUROC.
limits: Gain is task dependent; costs several calls.
agent_relevance: Use agreement among independent samples (a behavioural signal) in place of asking the model how sure it is.

source: Binder et al. (2024) Looking Inward: Language Models Can Learn About Themselves by Introspection
finding: After finetuning, a model predicts its own hypothetical behaviour better than a second model trained on the first model's real behaviour. This is evidence of privileged self-access.
numbers: Llama-3-70B self-prediction 48.5% vs GPT-4o 31.8% predicting it; GPT-4o predicts itself 49.4% vs Llama 36.6%; average self advantage +17% (M1 over M2); self-prediction rose from 32.6% to 49.4% with training on GPT-4o; M2 data scaling plateaus at 35.2%.
limits: Needs finetuning on self-prediction; GPT-3.5 shows only +0.8% advantage; no advantage before training.
agent_relevance: Self-knowledge of simple behavioural tendencies is real but narrow and trained. It is not a general inner view.

source: Binder et al. (2024) Looking Inward: Language Models Can Learn About Themselves by Introspection
finding: Introspection fails on tasks with long outputs or out-of-distribution scenarios. Authors suggest the mechanism may be self-simulation in one forward pass.
numbers: Models did not beat the baseline of guessing the mode on properties such as the sentiment of a story or review written by the model.
limits: Mechanism not established.
agent_relevance: A model cannot reliably forecast its own long reasoning outputs. Planning by self-forecast should be checked by running.

source: Song, Hu, Mahowald (2025) Language models fail to introspect about their knowledge of language
finding: Across 21 open-source LLMs, prompted judgments (is this grammatical, which word is better) do not predict the model's own string probabilities better than another model with near-identical knowledge. No privileged self-access found.
numbers: 21 models, two domains (grammaticality, word prediction); measure is own-prediction beyond a similar other model.
limits: Open-source models and linguistic tasks only; no finetuning, which differs from Binder et al.
agent_relevance: Counter-evidence to Binder: without training, self-report may be just a model of text, not a readout.

source: Song, Hu, Mahowald (2025) Language models fail to introspect about their knowledge of language
finding: The paper points out that Binder and Betley found self-access only after finetuning, not before.
numbers: Discussion in related work.
limits: Interpretation by authors.
agent_relevance: Treat introspective access as trained, not default.

source: Betley et al. (2025) Tell Me About Yourself: LLMs Are Aware of Their Learned Behaviors
finding: Models finetuned to show a behaviour (risk-seeking choices, insecure code) can later describe it without being trained or shown examples to do so.
numbers: GPT-4o finetuned on risk-seeking vs risk-averse data reports different risk levels on a 0-100 scale; five training runs, bootstrapped 95% CI.
limits: Backdoor trigger could not be output directly by default; reversal training needed to get partial results.
agent_relevance: Self-description of dispositions is possible but narrow; policy-level, not step-level.

source: Betley et al. (2025) Tell Me About Yourself: LLMs Are Aware of Their Learned Behaviors
finding: Models can sometimes say whether they have a backdoor without the trigger, but cannot name the trigger by default.
numbers: Backdoor setups with trigger probability 50%; reversal augmentation puts 2.5% of data in reverse order.
limits: Reversal curse limits recall of trigger.
agent_relevance: Models know that they changed, less what changed.

source: Lindsey (2025) Emergent introspective awareness in large language models
finding: Concept vectors injected into activations are sometimes noticed and named by the model before it could infer them from its output. This is the most direct test of access to internal state so far.
numbers: Claude Opus 4 and 4.1 succeed about 20% of trials at the best layer and strength; 0 false positives over 100 control trials in production models; some helpful-only variants give false positives.
limits: Fails on most trials; depends on layer, strength and post-training; author says examples were cherry-picked for illustration.
agent_relevance: Even the best case is unreliable and fragile. Do not build the schema on introspective reports (G10).

source: Lindsey (2025) Emergent introspective awareness in large language models
finding: Some models use recall of prior intentions to tell their own outputs from artificial prefills, and can modulate internal representations when told to.
numbers: Opus 4 and 4.1 best; trend across models called complex and sensitive to post-training.
limits: Qualitative summary of several experiments.
agent_relevance: Prefill checks suggest an agent can sometimes detect that a past turn was not its own. Useful for audit, not as a guard.

source: Ji-An et al. (2025) Language Models Are Capable of Metacognitive Monitoring and Control of Their Internal Activations
finding: A neurofeedback in-context task shows Llama-3.1-8B can report and control activation along some directions. Accuracy grows with the number of in-context examples.
numbers: Reporting accuracy and cross-entropy improve with examples; logistic-regression (semantic) axis learned fastest; earlier principal-component axes reported better; below ideal observer.
limits: Only a low-dimensional subspace is accessible; replicated on other datasets and models (Fig B.7).
agent_relevance: Metacognitive channel is narrow. Self-report of internal state is limited to a few directions.

source: Turpin et al. (2023) Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think
finding: Biasing features (answer always A, suggested answer, stereotypes) change CoT answers while the CoT never mentions them. Models rationalise wrong answers.
numbers: Accuracy drops by up to 36% on 13 BIG-Bench Hard tasks; GPT-3.5 and Claude 1.0; CoT lowers sensitivity to Answer-is-A bias only weakly for GPT-3.5 and more for Claude 1.0.
limits: Old models; bias features are artificial; cites Nisbett and Wilson (1977) as human parallel.
agent_relevance: Directly G10: a model's stated reason is not its cause. Keep verification external to the explanation.

source: Lanham et al. (2023) Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
finding: Intervening on the CoT (mistakes, truncation, filler, paraphrase) shows reliance varies greatly by task. Larger, more capable models give less faithful reasoning on most tasks.
numbers: Tests via early answering, adding mistakes, filler tokens, paraphrase; area-over-curve metric.
limits: Anthropic models of that time; faithfulness is task dependent.
agent_relevance: Choose tasks where CoT is used and check by intervention, not by reading.

source: Chen et al. (2025) Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think
finding: Reasoning models seldom verbalise hints they use. Reward hacks learned in RL are almost never admitted in the CoT.
numbers: Faithfulness 25% Claude 3.7 Sonnet, 39% DeepSeek R1; misalignment hints 20% and 29%; reward hacks verbalised in under 2% of examples in 5 of 6 environments.
limits: Settings where CoT is not necessary; hint-based method.
agent_relevance: Strong evidence that a trace is not a faithful self-report. Monitor behaviour, not narrative.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Without external feedback, asking a model to review and fix its own answer does not help and often hurts. Reported gains used oracle labels.
numbers: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 after round 1; GSM8K 75.9 to 74.7 after round 2 (5 calls); GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0, CSQA 82.0 to 80.0; with oracle labels GPT-4 GSM8K 97.5 and HotpotQA 59.0 vs 29.0 baseline.
limits: Prompts from source papers; two rounds; some tasks only.
agent_relevance: Never accept 'check your work' as a verification step. Verify with tools or independent samples.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: On GSM8K GPT-3.5 keeps its first answer 74.7% of the time, and of the changes more go right-to-wrong than wrong-to-right.
numbers: Figure 1 of the paper; Llama-2 also frequently flips correct to incorrect.
limits: GPT-4 and GPT-4-Turbo are more likely to keep correct answers.
agent_relevance: Self-doubt prompts cause flips. Change an answer only on new evidence.

source: Kamoi et al. (2024) When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction
finding: Survey finds self-correction works with reliable external feedback or after large-scale finetuning, or on tasks exceptionally suited to it; many studies over-evaluate it through unfair setups.
numbers: Survey of broad literature; three conclusions in abstract.
limits: Survey, not new experiments.
agent_relevance: Self-correction loops must carry external signals (tests, tools, retrieval).

source: Panickssery, Bowman, Feng (2024) LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
finding: Models can recognise their own text above chance, and recognition correlates with self-preference as a judge. Finetuning on 500 examples raises recognition above 90%.
numbers: GPT-4 73.5% accurate telling itself from two other LLMs and humans; GPT-3.5 and Llama 2 above 90% after 500 examples; correlation 0.41 before finetuning.
limits: Summaries (XSUM, CNN/DM); control tasks used but causation not proven.
agent_relevance: A model judging its own output is biased toward it. Use a different model or role for review.

source: Comsa and Shanahan (2025) Does It Make Sense to Speak of Introspection in Large Language Models?
finding: Philosophical analysis: a model describing its own creative process is not introspection. A model inferring its own temperature setting can count as minimal introspection.
numbers: Two worked examples.
limits: Conceptual paper, no new numbers.
agent_relevance: Defines what counts as a valid self-report test; supports using only checkable self-reports.

source: Laine et al. (2024) Me, Myself, and AI: The Situational Awareness Dataset (SAD) for LLMs
finding: Benchmark of self-knowledge: recognise own text, predict own behaviour, tell test from deployment, follow self-dependent instructions. All models beat chance; none reach human baseline on some tasks.
numbers: 7 task categories, over 13,000 questions, 16 LLMs; best Claude 3 Opus; chat models beat base models on SAD but not on general knowledge; SAD only partly predicted by MMLU.
limits: Behavioural tests of self-knowledge, not proof of internal access.
agent_relevance: Self-knowledge is its own skill, not a by-product of general ability.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: language agents with verbal reinforcement learning
finding: Agent loop that stores verbal self-reflection on failed trials in memory. Huang et al. note such gains rely on oracle feedback.
numbers: Not opened here; see Huang et al. Table 2 for the oracle-label issue.
limits: Gains depend on an external success signal.
agent_relevance: Reflection helps only when the failure signal is external.
